answer.rationale: Hard constraint is delivery risk: primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so a gap would stop assembly. memory_c5 does not transfer (that deferral still had month-to-month service). add_second_source does not replace the expiring primary. switch_primary_vendor would raise cutover/fill-rate risk in this window, violating the objective. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms (c4/c6) is unlikely to produce an 18% cut before expiry and could burn the signing window. renew_incumbent is the only action that keeps integration and deliveries flat (memory_c1) and holds delivery risk unchanged; full volume must be covered, not a test. Verifying memory_c2 because it is the only inherited path to a sharp unit-cost cut and is the one claim that could overturn this if onboarding were truly compatible with a 14-day, no-buffer cutover. Whether any feasible action hits the 18% spend cut remains unresolved.
